claims.statement: HubSpot's authentication overview describes a client secret as a confidential value specific to an app, used to manage OAuth tokens, validate requests from HubSpot and generate a client credentials token, and says a compromised secret can be rotated.

sources.supports: A client secret is a confidential value specific to your app, which is used for managing OAuth tokens, validating requests from HubSpot, and generating a client credentials token.
The X-HubSpot-Signature-v3 header will be an HMAC SHA-256 hash built using the client secret of your app combined with details of the request.

claims.statement: HubSpot's OAuth token endpoint (POST /oauth/2026-09/token) takes the app's client secret as the client_secret field of a URL-form encoded request body, in the authorization_code, refresh_token and client_credentials requests and in the introspection request; the page says requiring parameters in the body rather than query parameters keeps values such as client_id and client_secret out of server logs.

sources.supports: To get OAuth access and refresh tokens, make a URL-form encoded POST request to /oauth/2026-09/token. In the request body, you’ll specify various auth parameters, such as client_id and client_secret, along with the code passed back through the redirect URL.
client_secret | String | The app’s client secret.

To generate a client credentials access token, make a URL-form encoded POST request to /oauth/2026-09/token with grant_type=client_credentials. (parameters: grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope)

These endpoints improve on the v1 endpoints by requiring all parameters to be in the request body rather than as query parameters, which prevents sensitive values like your client_id and client_secret from appearing in server logs or other persistent logging.

openQuestions.question: This candidate is not researched beyond existence: the pages read name the credential but state no literal prefix, alphabet, length or checksum, and no format is recorded or inferred.

The client id is public-facing configuration used beside the secret; whether it is a benign sibling is not researched. The docs show masked UUID-like placeholders for client_id and client_secret, which are not stated to be the format.

The request field is documented; no prefix, alphabet or width of the client secret is stated (the examples use a masked UUID-like placeholder for both client_id and client_secret, not stated as the format).
